jess: quick one — our Node service in docker is getting 401s when calling the upstream api. inside the container process.env.API_KEY exists, but the Authorization header the upstream sees has trailing garbage. header I set is `Authorization: Basic ${Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':').toString('base64')}`
omar: do you mount the .env from a Windows host? that often adds CRLFs (``) which show up in base64 and break auth
jess: yes, volume mount from windows dev box. cat shows extra ^M at end. I didn't think a newline would matter since i append ':' then base64.
katie: newlines do matter — they change the bytes before base64. quick fixes: `process.env.API_KEY = process.env.API_KEY && process.env.API_KEY.trim()` or when reading secret file: `fs.readFileSync('/run/secrets/api_key','utf8').replace(/|
/g,'')`
omar: if you want a container-level fix, add a tiny entrypoint step: `sed -i 's/$//' /run/secrets/api_key || true` or `dos2unix` during image build. also check `.gitattributes/core.autocrlf` if the file comes from repo
jess: ah got it — trimming in startup fixed it locally, tests pass. thanks.
devex-bot: FYI — we have a short internal note on secret mounting gotchas (CRLFs, trailing newlines, file vs env mounts) in the devex repo; ping @katie if you want it linked in the README :thumbsup:
jess: pinging to add to our service README so next person doesn't fall into this. :raised_hands:
